Expectation: Board and senior management accountability: the board approves an AI strategy with the approach and risk appetite; roles across the three lines for approval and monitoring; regular review by senior management
What the wiki does not cover: The wiki has no control or test case on board understanding of AI or on quantitative risk appetite measures

Expectation: Use-case owners and human oversight: a named owner for each use case; in-the-loop, on-the-loop or in-command oversight with risk-based triggers; reviewers able to challenge, override or stop; oversight tested
Inventory: an up-to-date inventory of approved use cases including third-party and embedded AI, with standard attributes; unlisted AI restricted; shadow AI controlled

Risk-commensurate management: materiality and risk assessment sets the review depth; senior sign-off, independent validation and adversarial testing for material cases; end-to-end testing; tailored monitoring; fallback, recovery and a kill switch or equivalent; auditable records and outcome tracing
What the wiki does not cover: The wiki gates release on a security review; independent statistical model validation is outside its scope

Expectation: Risk management frameworks: data within approved parameters and PDPO compliance, contracts that stop providers training on data without authorisation, masking; third-party due diligence, contracts, monitoring, concentration and exit; layered cyber controls against data poisoning and prompt injection
Resources and expertise: adequate resources and capacity; organisation-wide awareness; role-specific training
Accountability for outputs: controls against hallucination; stronger review where customers could be materially affected; rules for withholding, referring or blocking outputs
Explainability and transparency: document explainability and its limits; inform stakeholders of purpose, functions, limits and the basis of material outcomes; prefer more explainable arrangements

Ethical use and fair treatment: no unfair bias; monitoring and sampling of customer-affecting outputs; clarification, review and redress; tell consumers about AI use and its risks before service; existing disclosure and opt-out expectations continue
